summary: Router 0.39.0: the session store is chosen by the scheme of its URL (implements ADR-0114 from #177; ADR-0122 proposed). postgresql:// and postgres:// open the unchanged PostgresSessionStore (asyncpg already accepted only these schemes, so no existing installation changes); sqlite:///<file> opens a new SqliteSessionStore in router.state_dir (absolute with sqlite:////...). Any other scheme, a SQLite URL with a query, fragment, '..', a control character or :memory: is a fixed 400 Problem before anything opens; the URL never appears in a Problem, log line or posture finding (a PostgreSQL URL may carry a password). B4 (router <-> session store): the SQLite store reuses CoreStore/ManagedStore/ReliabilityStore/ExchangeStore unchanged (create/get/update/delete/append/read moved verbatim from PostgresSessionStore into CoreStore), so every owner-scoped WHERE clause, lease check, idempotency comparison and deletion-lifecycle step is the same code on both engines; sqlite_store.translate rewrites only fixed server statements (parameters stay bound, never interpolated; the cache key is the constant SQL text). Concurrency: one connection used by one worker thread, one asyncio lock per call, BEGIN IMMEDIATE per call; cancellation/timeouts queue the rollback in the same FIFO thread before the next BEGIN, so no transaction is shared between callers (tested: timeout and cancellation while another process holds the file lock, the next call sees no leftovers). A second process on the same file serializes on the file lock (busy_timeout = timeout_s). Isolation is verified by the same two-principal contract tests on both engines, through the HTTP API too. File: created 0600 via os.open with O_NOFOLLOW where available (a symlink in place of the file is refused), an existing file and its -wal/-shm/-journal companions are chmod 0600 at every start (ADR-0056 spirit); the router unit's UMask=0077 applies too. trusted_schema=OFF so a tampered file cannot make triggers/views call application functions (our triggers use none; Unicode lower/clock functions are only used in top-level statements); STRICT tables and json_valid checks reject wrongly typed values; foreign keys on (cascade delete). Driver/file faults stay at the existing `database` boundary (fixed UNAVAILABLE); startup logs only class, errno and SQLite error name. B4/B5 deletion and restore (TM-12, ADR-0076): delete/cleanup/replay_deletions/outbox_* are the shared mixin code, the deletion journal replay runs unchanged at start before the outbox worker; tested on SQLite: session delete with/without memory, deletion requested in flight, retention, simulated restore + replay, stuck/reconcile listing, and a real file backup (sqlite3 backup API) restored over the store file then replayed (session gone, pending send marked deleted without payload). secure_delete=ON overwrites deleted rows in the database file (tested: a deleted marker is absent from the file after close); older page versions remain in the -wal file until the next checkpoint and in backups (documented, comparable to PostgreSQL dead tuples/WAL). B9: posture reports session_store_url_unsupported (medium, URL not printed), session_store_sqlite_file (info: path and mode, backup command) and session_store_file_readable (medium, POSIX mode & 077). No new route, auth path, network listener, egress or dependency (stdlib sqlite3; no lock change). Memory outbox: OutboxStore is now its own Protocol; memory.py still takes the session store as outbox, so outbox_enabled still requires session_store.enabled, now on either engine. Tests changed: the four integration files run one contract class per engine via test/store_engines.py; selftests using a patched PostgresSessionStore.open now set a postgresql:// shaped synthetic DSN (the factory refuses scheme-less values). CI: the SQLite halves are added to the python job; the sessions-postgres job keeps its name (required check) and runs both engines. Re-reviewed after merging origin/main (first portability wave, ADR-0101..0120 incl. ADR-0114 proposed, and #185 router container image, router 0.38.0, ADR-0121) into the branch: conflicts only in CHANGELOG (v0.44.0 on top), VERSION (0.39.0), ADR index (regenerated, now gap-free 0001-0122), the install-router package row (both sides kept), AGENTS.md (container rules plus both-engine integrations) and this record. The image copies the whole skirnir_router package, so the new modules ship in it; sqlite3 is in its Python. Checked inside the built image (Python 3.14, SQLite 3.46.1): the 20 SQLite contract tests pass as user 10001, and with --read-only, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges and a state volume the store opens sqlite:///sessions.db in /var/lib/skirnir-router, writes, and the file is 0600 owned by 10001. compose.yaml and install-router (EN/DE) name sqlite:/// as the single-host option. ADR-0114 stays proposed: repository practice accepts ADRs in a separate maintainer PR (e.g. ADR-0098..0100). Re-reviewed after a CI failure of test_parallel_first_start_on_a_new_file (SQLITE_BUSY for one of several openers of a new file). Two real first-start races were found with a stress script (8-16 parallel openers on a new file, 200-300 rounds, also with random 0-20 ms delays between setup statements; before the fix 19/100 rounds failed on Windows and 30-48/200 in WSL): (1) PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL on a new file needs the exclusive lock and SQLite answers a concurrent opener with SQLITE_BUSY without the busy handler, or keeps the old mode; switch_to_wal now asks again with a jittered pause until the mode is wal or timeout_s passed, telling BUSY apart only by sqlite_errorcode (never the message), other faults and a lasting lock still reach the startup boundary (fixed 503). (2) tighten_companions checked for -wal/-shm/-journal and then chmod-ed, racing with SQLite removing them (FileNotFoundError); it now opens -wal/-shm with O_NOFOLLOW and fchmods, treating only FileNotFoundError as 'not there' (a symlinked WAL file is refused like a symlinked database file); the transient rollback journal is no longer touched. busy_timeout is now the first statement on every connection. Security effect: no new input path; the retry is bounded by timeout_s and only for the store's own file at startup. The test closes every opener (8 instead of 4) and asyncTearDown skips cleanup when the store is a Problem or already closed.

limitations: Deleted content can remain in the -wal file until the next checkpoint (about 4 MiB of writes, or router stop) and in backups; documented in design/session-store.md, comparable to PostgreSQL dead tuples and WAL segments.

The symlink check (O_NOFOLLOW) happens when the router creates/opens the file; sqlite3.connect opens the path again afterwards, and the -wal/-shm files are opened by SQLite itself. Exploiting that gap needs write access to the router's state folder, which already means control of the router's files.
The whole SQLite store is one writer at a time; a slow call (large history read) delays others up to timeout_s, then they answer 503.
ADR-0114's separate outbox-only store is not implemented; the outbox remains in the session store (now on either engine).
Not tested on a real router host or with a large SQLite file; CI covers Linux, Windows was used for development runs.
test/smoke_container.sh was not run locally (Windows host); CI's container job runs it, including the router self-tests inside the image.
